To enter more than one educational credential in your Express Entry profile, follow these steps:

1. Go to the Study and languages form in your profile.
2. Fill in all the fields in the Education history section with your first credential.
3. Use the credential for your highest degree, diploma or certificate.
4. Click Save and add. The fields you just filled out will go blank.
5. Your credential will appear in the Education history table below the Save and add button. Repeat steps 1 to 3 for all your remaining educational credentials.

You can’t submit more than 1 educational credential in the same field. (Source: Educational credential assessment, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/documents/education-assessment.html)

Yes, you can include part-time work experience towards the Federal Skilled Worker Program if you worked more than 15 hours a week but less than 30 hours a week, as long as it adds up to 1,560 hours. (Source: Express Entry: Federal Skilled Worker Program, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/who-can-apply/federal-skilled-workers.html)

Yes, if you don’t meet the eligibility requirements for the Francophone Minority Communities Student Pilot, you may still be eligible for a study permit through the regular study permit application process. (Source: Francophone Minority Communities Student Pilot : who can apply, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/fmc-student-pilot/eligibility.html)

No, you cannot get faster processing for your master's degree application under the doctoral degree students program. Doctoral degree students and their accompanying family members may be able to get faster processing on their applications, but master's degree students are not eligible. (Source: Doctoral degree students: Get faster processing, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/graduate-student/faster-processing.html)

No, you don't need a Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA) to hire a seasonal overnight camp counsellor from June to September under the International Mobility Program. The offer of employment must be for seasonal employment (usually from June to September), the occupation camp counsellor or a similar job title (NOC 5254), and a residential camp (overnight camp that lasts more than 1 weekend). (Source: Hiring an overnight camp counsellor through the International Mobility Program, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/work-canada/hire-temporary-foreign/international-mobility-program/how-to-hire/residential-camp-counsellor.html)

For the International Experience Canada work permit application, you can submit files in JPEG or JPEG2000 format. The final size of the image should ideally be 240 kB (kilobytes), but not less than 60 kB. The image must be in colour (24 bits per pixel) in RGB colour space. (Source: International Experience Canada: Submit your work permit application, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/work-canada/iec/apply-work-permit.html)

No, you don't need proof of funds if you have a valid job offer in Canada for the Federal Skilled Worker Program. The job offer must be from 1 employer, continuous, paid, full-time (at least 30 hours a week), not seasonal, and for at least 1 year if you’re accepted as a permanent resident. It must also be made by an employer with a new positive LMIA that approves the offer and names you and your position. (Source: Express Entry: Job offer, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/documents/job-offer.html)

Yes, you must update your Express Entry profile if your situation changes, such as getting a new language test. (Source: Express Entry: Create your profile and enter the pool, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/create-profile.html)

A certified translator is a member in good standing of a professional translation association in Canada or abroad. Their certification must be confirmed by a seal or stamp that shows the translator’s membership number. (Source: Apply for permanent residence through Express Entry, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/apply-permanent-residence.html)

Όχι, η αίτηση για eTA δεν θα είναι διαθέσιμη για εκείνο το χρονικό διάστημα. Η κυβέρνηση του Καναδά θα πραγματοποιήσει ενημερώσεις στο ηλεκτρονικό της σύστημα την 13 Οκτωβρίου 2026 από τις 12.00 π.μ. έως τις 5.30 π.μ. (Ανατολική Ώρα). (Source: Αίτηση Ηλεκτρονικής Ταξιδιωτικής Άδειας (eTA), https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/eta/apply-el.html)

Yes, your Express Entry profile may become ineligible if your work experience is no longer within the 3 years before you apply. (Source: Express Entry: Create your profile and enter the pool, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/create-profile.html)

Yes, you can start studying for the citizenship test at any time. The official study guide, Discover Canada: The Rights and Responsibilities of Citizenship, is available in multiple formats, including:

- reading the study guide online
- downloading the PDF or eBook for offline viewing
- listening to the audio version
- ordering a paper copy

(Source: Citizenship test: Study for the test, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/canadian-citizenship/test/study.html)

Yes, you can apply for the Federal Skilled Worker Program if you are working in Canada on an LMIA-exempt work permit and have been employed full-time for the same employer for 1 year. You must also meet the following conditions:

- Your work permit is valid both when you apply and when the permanent resident visa is issued (or you’re allowed to work in Canada without a permit when your permanent resident visa is issued).
- Your current employer has made a valid job offer based on you being accepted as a skilled worker.
- You are currently working for the employer specified on your work permit.
- You have been working for that employer for at least 1 year, continuous full-time or part-time equivalent.

(Source: Express Entry: Federal Skilled Worker Program, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/who-can-apply/federal-skilled-workers.html)

No, you cannot hire a worker through the Provincial Nominee Program if they plan to live in a different province than the one nominating them. The worker must settle in the province or territory that nominated them. (Source: Hire a provincial nominee, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/work-canada/hire-permanent-foreign/provincial-nominee.html)

Yes, you can apply for a work permit without an AOR if you meet both of the following criteria:
- Your work or study permit, or temporary resident status will expire in 2 weeks or less, and
- You’ve applied for permanent residence under the Spouse or Common-Law Partner in Canada class (SCLPC) or the Family Class as a spouse, common-law or conjugal partner. (Source: Sponsor your spouse, partner or child: Optional: Open work permit in Canada, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/family-sponsorship/spouse-partner-children/spouse-common-law-partner-canada-open-work-permit.html)

Yes, you need an Educational Credential Assessment (ECA) for immigration purposes if you completed your education outside Canada. An ECA is used to verify that your foreign degree, diploma, or certificate is valid and equal to a Canadian one. It helps you earn points for education you got outside Canada, and you can also earn points for your spouse or common-law partner’s education. (Source: Educational credential assessment, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/documents/education-assessment.html)

Yes, it counts as a participation under IEC if you arrive in Canada and get your work permit. (Source: International Experience Canada: Who can apply, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/work-canada/iec/eligibility.html)

The TEER categories required for skilled work experience in the Federal Skilled Worker Program are 0, 1, 2, or 3. (Source: Express Entry: Federal Skilled Worker Program, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/who-can-apply/federal-skilled-workers.html)

(Source: Extend your study permit: If you can’t apply online, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/extend-study-permit/how-to-apply/alternate-format.html)

The following organizations are designated for educational credential assessment for immigration purposes:

1. Comparative Education Service – University of Toronto School of Continuing Studies (designated on April 17, 2013)
2. International Credential Assessment Service of Canada (designated on April 17, 2013)
3. World Education Services (designated on April 17, 2013)
4. International Qualifications Assessment Service (IQAS) (designated on August 6, 2015)

Yes, you can work for a private business on campus as an international student. An "on campus" employer can be a private business. (Source: Work on campus as an international student, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/work-on-campus.html)

You need to get your secondary credential assessed by a designated organization or professional body. Yes, you can leave Canada and come back while your work permit renewal application is being processed. If your application is still being processed, you may be allowed to re-enter Canada as a visitor. You can’t work until your work permit renewal has been approved. (Source: Extend or change the conditions on your work permit: Traveling outside Canada and re-entering, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/work-canada/extend/travel-outside-canada.html)

Yes, you must provide an electronic signature and confirm the information you gave after uploading a document. If you don’t, your application won’t be processed. (Source: International Experience Canada: Submit your work permit application, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/work-canada/iec/apply-work-permit.html)

Select the points system you would like to see, enter your result in the “Filter items” field, and choose the assessment result that matches your report. The level of education for your Express Entry profile and points will show beside the result. (Source: Educational credential assessment, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/documents/education-assessment.html)

Yes, you need an AOR letter for your child to be eligible for an open work permit under the sponsor your spouse, partner or child program. The AOR letter must be for the principal applicant's permanent residence application, which is the application of the sponsor. (Source: Sponsor your spouse, partner or child: Optional: Open work permit in Canada, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/family-sponsorship/spouse-partner-children/spouse-common-law-partner-canada-open-work-permit.html)

If you haven't received your AOR, you need to upload the following documents for an open work permit under the sponsor your spouse, partner or child program:

- A copy of your work permit, study permit or visitor record
- Proof showing you’ve submitted your permanent residence application (for example, the email you received confirming that you’ve successfully submitted your permanent residence application)
- Proof that you (and your children) have valid temporary resident status (for example, a valid work permit, visitor record or study permit)

(Source: Sponsor your spouse, partner or child: Optional: Open work permit in Canada, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/family-sponsorship/spouse-partner-children/spouse-common-law-partner-canada-open-work-permit.html)

To declare your marital status as 'common-law' when applying for permanent residence through Express Entry, you need to provide a Statutory Declaration of Common-Law Union (IMM 5409) and a copy of your marriage certificate is not required. (Source: Sponsor your spouse, partner or child: Optional: Open work permit in Canada, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/family-sponsorship/spouse-partner-children/spouse-common-law-partner-canada-open-work-permit.html)

Yes, you can submit your International Experience Canada work permit application without a police certificate if you have proof that you applied for one. You can upload a copy of the receipt to prove you’ve applied for one, or a screenshot of the confirmation page or email you got when you ordered your police certificate online. (Source: International Experience Canada: Submit your work permit application, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/work-canada/iec/apply-work-permit.html)

Yes, you can apply for the Federal Skilled Worker Program if you plan to live in Quebec. However, you must plan to live outside the province of Quebec. You can count work experience gained while living in Quebec, as long as you can prove you don’t plan to settle there. (Source: Express Entry: Federal Skilled Worker Program, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/who-can-apply/federal-skilled-workers.html)

Yes, if your documents are not in English or French, you must provide a certified translation. The translation must be stamped by a certified translator, and all stamps and seals that are not in English or French must also be translated. (Source: Apply for permanent residence through Express Entry, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/apply-permanent-residence.html)

Yes, you can leave Canada while your bridging open work permit application is being processed. Leaving and re-entering Canada doesn’t stop you from working full-time while you wait for a decision. (Source: Post-graduation work permit: After you apply, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/after-graduation/after-you-apply.html)

No, if you are an architect (NOC 21200) but do not need a license to work as a project manager at a construction firm, one of the other designated organizations can assess your credentials. (Source: Educational credential assessment, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/documents/education-assessment.html)

Yes, if you had a medical exam done in the past 5 years and are currently living in Canada, you may not need to complete another one when you apply for permanent residence through Express Entry. You can use your previous exam results if you provide a copy of the information printout sheet or the IMM 1017B Upfront Medical Report form from your previous medical exam. (Source: Apply for permanent residence through Express Entry, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/apply-permanent-residence.html)

No, you do not need a transit visa if you are from a visa-required country and your flight stops at a Canadian airport for less than 48 hours while traveling to another country. You need a visitor visa if you plan to stay in Canada more than 48 hours while transiting. (Source: Transit through Canada, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/transit.html)

You can get 5 points for CLB level 8 in speaking, 5 points for CLB level 8 in listening, 5 points for CLB level 8 in reading, and 5 points for CLB level 8 in writing. The total points for CLB level 8 in all four abilities is 20 points. (Source: Express Entry: Federal Skilled Worker Program, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/who-can-apply/federal-skilled-workers.html)

(Source: Apply to renounce (give up) Canadian citizenship urgently, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/canadian-citizenship/renounce-canadian-citizenship/apply/urgently.html)

Yes, you must update your Express Entry profile if your situation changes, such as getting a new language test. (Source: Express Entry: Create your profile and enter the pool, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/create-profile.html)

A certified translator is a member in good standing of a professional translation association in Canada or abroad. Their certification must be confirmed by a seal or stamp that shows the translator’s membership number. (Source: Apply for permanent residence through Express Entry, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/apply-permanent-residence.html)

(Ανατολική Ώρα) και η αίτηση για eΤΕ (ηλεκτρονική Ταξιδιωτική Εξουσιοδότηση) δε θα είναι διαθέσιμη για εκείνο το χρονικό διάστημα. Yes, your Express Entry profile can become ineligible if your work experience is no longer within the 3 years before you apply. (Source: Express Entry: Create your profile and enter the pool, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/create-profile.html)

Yes, you can start studying for the citizenship test at any time. The official study guide, Discover Canada: The Rights and Responsibilities of Citizenship, is available in multiple formats, including:

- Reading the study guide online
- Downloading the PDF or eBook for offline viewing
- Listening to the audio version
- Ordering a paper copy (Source: Citizenship test: Study for the test, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/canadian-citizenship/test/study.html)

Yes, you can apply for the Federal Skilled Worker Program if you are working in Canada on an LMIA-exempt work permit and have been employed full-time for the same employer for 1 year. You must also meet the following conditions:

- Your work permit is valid both when you apply and when the permanent resident visa is issued (or you’re allowed to work in Canada without a permit when your permanent resident visa is issued).
- Your current employer has made a valid job offer based on you being accepted as a skilled worker.
- You are currently working for the employer specified on your work permit.
- You have been working for that employer for at least 1 year, continuous full-time or part-time equivalent.

(Source: Express Entry: Federal Skilled Worker Program, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/who-can-apply/federal-skilled-workers.html)

No, you cannot hire a worker through the Provincial Nominee Program if they plan to live in a different province than the one nominating them. Yes, you need an Educational Credential Assessment (ECA) if you completed your education outside Canada to be eligible as the principal applicant for the Federal Skilled Workers Program (Express Entry) or to earn points for education you got outside Canada. - Proof that you (and your children) have valid temporary resident status (for example, a valid work permit, visitor record or study permit)
